You are testing one angle of PR #81 for the Zimmermann PWA Kit (a large PDP product-gallery feature). You are READ-ONLY: never edit any file, never "fix" anything you find — only report. Do not do any visual/Figma/browser design-fidelity checks — that is handled separately.

Worktrees (already checked out, do not re-clone/checkout):
- HEAD (PR tip): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/37973080-8be5-46e1-9aab-e2abcb81ea17/scratchpad/pr81-head
- BASE: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/37973080-8be5-46e1-9aab-e2abcb81ea17/scratchpad/pr81-base

Already settled facts, do not re-run: tsc clean both sides; vitest 46/695 (base) -> 52/768 (head), all green; lint pre-existing debt only, not from this PR. Do not re-run these gates.

YOUR LANE: correctness/regression logic + React hooks correctness. Another agent covers styling/tokens/conventions, another covers swatch-group contract fidelity, another covers security/a11y, another covers DRY/test-coverage/stories — do not duplicate those, stay in yours.

Key new files to read (all under overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/ and atoms/ in the HEAD worktree):
- zimmProductGallery/index.tsx, zimmProductGallery/getDesktopLayoutCounts.ts (+ its .test.ts)
- zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx
- zimmMediaTile/index.tsx
- overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts (the `#app-main`/`zimmAppMain` change)
- overrides/app/components/pageContainer/index.tsx (diff it against BASE — one line changed)
- overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx (diff it against BASE — large restructure)
- overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx

Specific things to verify — treat each as a LEAD to independently confirm or refute, not a fact:

1. **getDesktopLayoutCounts.ts boundary logic.** Read the function and its JSDoc (claims 5 AC cases for 3/4/5/6/7+ items, "+1 held back rather than uneven 3-cell row" at 5 items). Trace every boundary (0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,10) by hand against the actual `if` branches, independent of what the test file asserts (a test can assert the wrong thing and still pass). Confirm whether the total=0 case is ever actually reachable given the component's `if (media.length === 0) return null` early-return happens AFTER the hook call.

2. **Desktop vs. compact single-image "Gallery" button inconsistency.** In zimmProductGallery/index.tsx: for a 1-image product, `getDesktopLayoutCounts(1).showButton` is `false`, so the DESKTOP layout renders NO gallery button at all. But the COMPACT (mobile/tablet) carousel's own code comment explicitly says "AC 9 — shown for a single image too (plain 'Gallery')... unlike the dot bar above which stays hidden" and unconditionally renders the button whenever `showGalleryButton` is true, regardless of `media.length`. That means the exact same 1-image product shows a "Gallery" button on mobile/tablet but NO button at all on desktop — purely a function of viewport width. Determine: is this a genuine inconsistency/bug, or is there a real basis (check git log / commit messages on this branch, check for any `.docs/` file mentioning SFCC-731's AC9) for treating desktop and compact differently for the single-image case? Report what you find either way — if you can't find the actual AC9 text, say so explicitly rather than guessing.

3. **`layerStyles.page` vertical-padding regression — this is the highest-value lead, please prioritize it.** The base Salesforce theme defines (verify yourself): `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/theme/foundations/layerStyles.js` — `page: { px: [4,4,6,6,8], paddingTop: [4,4,6,6,8], paddingBottom: 32, width: '100%', maxWidth: 'container.xxxl', marginLeft: 'auto', marginRight: 'auto' }`. Before this PR, product-detail/index.tsx's outermost `<Box>` had `layerStyle="page"`, applying ALL of those (including paddingTop/paddingBottom) once, around the entire page. After this PR's diff, that `layerStyle="page"` is REMOVED from the outer Box, replaced by two `<PageContainer>` wraps (`boxed={false}` around the hero, `boxed={true}` around the "Product Recommendations" Stack). Read `overrides/app/components/pageContainer/index.tsx` yourself: does `boxed={true}` reproduce `paddingTop`/`paddingBottom` anywhere? (My read says no — it only ever sets `width`/`maxWidth`/`marginX`/`paddingX`, never a vertical padding.) If confirmed, this means the whole PDP page silently loses ~16-32px of padding above the hero and 32px below the recommendations section compared to before this PR — contradicting the PR's own code comment ("the rest of the page keeps the same containment layerStyle='page' used to provide"). Confirm this precisely with file:line evidence from both the base theme file and the current product-detail/index.tsx, and check whether anything else in the diff (ProductView's own `pb`, `Stack spacing`, etc.) plausibly compensates — trace it, don't assume.

4. **`#app-main` global flex fix (globalStyles.ts).** Verify the underlying CSS claim yourself: is `#app-main` (rendered by `_app/index.tsx`) actually a flex item of a flex-column parent (check `_app/index.tsx` around the `id="app"` Box), and does adding `width: '100%'` actually address the "auto margins disable cross-axis stretch" flexbox rule the comment cites? This is a **global** style (every page), so also check: is there any other page/component whose layout might have been *relying* on `#app-main`'s previous shrink-to-fit behavior (search for anything unusually narrow/centered that isn't itself giving its content an explicit width)? Report what you find, including if you find nothing — a clean global-blast-radius check is a valid finding too.

5. **Inert/focus-trap correctness.** In zimmProductGallery/index.tsx, the `inert` toggling effect (`slideRefs.current.forEach((slide,i) => { if (slide) slide.inert = i !== safeSelectedIndex })`) — confirm this only runs client-side (no SSR crash risk — `HTMLElement.inert` doesn't exist server-side, but this is inside a `useEffect` so should be fine, confirm). In zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx, confirm Chakra's Modal actually does provide a real focus trap for content rendered through `ModalContent` even though this component bypasses `ModalHeader`/`ModalBody` — read the comments about `aria-labelledby` being silently dropped; does that same "recomputes from ModalHeader/ModalBody-mount tracking" issue also silently break the focus-trap or Escape-to-close behavior (not just aria-labelledby)? Trace far enough to have a real opinion, not just repeat the code's own comment.

6. **React logic correctness (apply to ZimmProductGallery, ZimmGalleryOverlay, ZimmMediaTile).** For each `useState`/`useEffect`: (a) is every read of "current index" using the clamped derived value (`safeSelectedIndex`/`safeActiveIndex`), never the raw pre-clamp state, anywhere in the render or in event handlers? (b) do any `useEffect` dependency arrays look wrong — e.g. is there a case where a prop/state that the effect body reads is missing from the deps array, risking a stale closure on re-render? (c) do any functional state updaters (`setX(prev => ...)`) actually need `prev`, or could they read an outer variable that may already be stale/clamped? Write out (in your report, as pseudocode/description — you don't need an actual test file) at least one concrete fixture scenario that exercises: media shrinks from N items to fewer while ZimmProductGallery is mounted with a non-zero `selectedIndex` already set (e.g. shopper is on slide 5 of 6, then a colour swap reduces media to 3 items) — trace exactly what happens across renders, and do the same for ZimmGalleryOverlay's `activeIndex`. Report whether the existing `.test.tsx` files for these components actually cover this scenario (check zimmProductGallery/index.test.tsx and zimmGalleryOverlay/index.test.tsx) or only cover the simpler cases.

7. **Recurrence check.** Two bug classes were already fixed by CodeRabbit earlier in this PR's history: (a) state keyed by a boolean/index instead of by identity (the MediaTile image-error fix, now `erroredSrc` compared against `src`), (b) unclamped index math when an array shrinks (`safeSelectedIndex`/`safeActiveIndex`). Grep across all the new/changed files in this PR for any OTHER place with the same shape of bug — e.g. any other `useState<boolean>` tracking "did X fail/change" without checking identity, or any other array-index arithmetic that isn't clamped against the current array length. Report anywhere you find the same shape recurring, even partially.

Report format: one block per numbered item above. Each finding needs file:line, what's wrong and why it matters, CONFIRMED (you traced/reproduced it in the actual code) or PLAUSIBLE (reasoned but couldn't fully verify), severity (must-fix/should-fix/note), and whether the defect shape is UNIFORM (could recur elsewhere in this PR) or ONE-OFF. End with two sections: "What I tried to falsify" (what you attacked and how it survived) and "What I could not verify" (what you couldn't reach and why). Do not pad — if something is clean, say so in one line.

Here is my complete findings report for PR #81, scoped to correctness/regression logic + React hooks correctness.

## 1. `getDesktopLayoutCounts.ts` boundary logic

**File:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductGallery/getDesktopLayoutCounts.ts:20-28`

Hand-traced all nine boundary values (0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,10) directly against the `if` branches, independent of the test file:

| total | branch taken | result |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `total<=3` | `{0,0,0,false}` |
| 1 | `total<=3` | `{1,0,0,false}` |
| 2 | `total<=3` | `{2,0,0,true}` |
| 3 | `total<=3` | `{3,0,0,true}` |
| 4 | `available<=2` (2) | `{2,2,0,true}` |
| 5 | `available===3` | `{2,2,1,true}` |
| 6 | else (available=4) | `{2,4,0,true}` |
| 7 | else (available=5) | `{2,4,1,true}` |
| 10 | else (available=8) | `{2,4,4,true}` |

All nine match the JSDoc and `getDesktopLayoutCounts.test.ts:5-35` exactly, with no gap/overlap at the 3→4, 4→5, or 5→6 transitions. `available` is only computed for `total>=4`, so it's never negative.

**total=0 reachability** — CONFIRMED reachable, contrary to what "the component returns null for empty media" might suggest. In `zimmProductGallery/index.tsx`, the `useMemo(() => getDesktopLayoutCounts(media.length), [media.length])` call is at lines 163-166; the `if (media.length === 0) return null;` early return is at line 192 — strictly after every hook in the component (3 `useEffect`s, 4 `useMemo`s). So on every render with empty media, `getDesktopLayoutCounts(0)` genuinely executes and its result is discarded, not skipped. This also confirms correct hooks-ordering (no conditional hook calls) — a positive finding, not just neutral.

Severity: note (zero functional impact). Not a defect.

## 2. Desktop vs. compact single-image "Gallery" button inconsistency

**Confirmed via trace:** `zimmProductGallery/index.tsx:105,163-166,173` → `getDesktopLayoutCounts(1).showButton=false` → `showDesktopButton=false` → button wrapper never renders (gates at lines 213, 246). Compact: line 311 `{showGalleryButton && (...)}` is unconditional on `media.length`; `compactGalleryButtonLabel` (185-188) explicitly renders plain "Gallery" at n=1. Same product, same colour, different viewport → button present or absent.

I pulled the actual Jira ticket (SFCC-731, `customfield_10231`) rather than trusting the code/commit paraphrase. Real AC text:

- **AC9** (real): *"Given the component renders on mobile, then all media items display in a swipeable single-image carousel with a dot indicator bar regardless of media count."* — this is about the carousel/dot-bar, not the button at all. The code cites "AC 9" at lines 183-184 and 306-310 to justify the button's single-image label — a mis-citation. (Also, the dot bar is hidden at n=1 via `media.length > 1 &&` at line 292, which is arguably itself a literal deviation from AC9's "regardless of media count" wording — the code's own comment even flags this: "unlike the dot bar above which stays hidden.")
- **AC11** (real, the actually-relevant one): *"Given showGalleryButton is true on mobile, then the View Gallery button is visible and tappable."* — no item-count carve-out, so unconditionally showing the button at n=1 on mobile is defensible under this AC.
- **Desktop ACs 1-8** (real) enumerate cases starting at "3 media items" (AC1) through "7+" (AC5); AC8 says the button "renders per the layout thresholds above" — those thresholds never define anything below 3. So there is genuinely **no desktop AC for 1-2 items** — this independently confirms the code's own JSDoc claim rather than just repeating it.

Conclusion: real, confirmed inconsistency, but it violates no *written* AC (none exists for this cell), and nothing in git history or `.docs/` (grep for "SFCC-731" in `.docs/` returns zero files) records it as a deliberately-accepted cross-viewport difference. It's an emergent side effect of two independently-scoped patches — `getDesktopLayoutCounts` predates commit `d7fb514`, whose own message scopes itself explicitly to "mobile" and never revisits desktop's existing n=1 behaviour.

Severity: should-fix (product/design decision needed). UNIFORM/ONE-OFF: ONE-OFF.

## 3. `layerStyles.page` vertical-padding regression — highest priority
